text:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT (P1) - 504 / 5xx surge on private-inference-gw (eu-west-1). Error rate crossed 10% for 3m. Paging oncall. Link: https://metrics.redwood/example/alerts/2009876543 :rotating_light:

Alex: Seeing ~30% 504s from inference-gateway egress to customer backends. Traffic shows heavy short-lived flows. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/eu-west-1/gateway/egress

Maria: Confirming — NAT gateway SNAT port utilization near 100% for the private subnets. Metric: ephemeral_ports_in_use=64350 / 65536. Getting lots of TIME_WAIT from downstream.

Ryan (oncall): I'm on it. Brief status: assessing whether this is NAT port exhaustion, conntrack limits, or peering blackholes. Can someone grab NAT metrics and vpc flow logs for the last 10m?

Jen (netops): NAT gateway metrics attached. Also seeing high retransmits and a burst of short TCP sessions. Peering routes look stable, BGP shows no flap. Starting with conntrack and SNAT pool checks.

Sophia: Copy. From an app perspective customers report requests stuck ~1-2s then 504. We have retries which are amplifying the burst. Recommending temporary client-side throttle and disable aggressive retries for public customers.

Alex: Quick check I ran from an instance in the private subnet:
```
$ ss -s
TCP:   64000 established,  2000 closed,  56000 orphaned,  1200 timewait

$ sudo conntrack -S | head
conntrack events: 0
entries: 65000

# /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_conntrack_max = 65536
```
This looks like conntrack / ephemeral port exhaustion.

Ryan (oncall): Thanks. Action plan: 1) Throttle retries at edge (NGINX) for affected routes. 2) Temporarily move affected customers to hosted egress (public) via policy. 3) Add second NAT gateway in same AZ and enable port-range pooling on egress proxy as short-term. 4) Netops to investigate conntrack timeouts and kernel tuning.

Jen (netops): I can spin up a second NAT gateway in the VPC and update route table to include it. Also we can enable a pool of static SNAT ports on our egress proxy. Starting now. ETA 6m.

Customer SRE: We're seeing ~18% errors for requests to the model endpoint. Customer impact: multiple customers in EU region (cust-42, cust-77) flagged. They're on private deployment. They asked for immediate mitigation and a status update to their oncall.

Alex: Initiated a canary failover for the most impacted tenant (cust-42) to the hosted inference endpoint. We observed drop in errors for that tenant to <1%. Rolling to cust-77 next if second NAT bootstraps cleanly.

Maria: Netops confirms second NAT gw created. Route table updated to use both NATs via subsets. SNAT port usage dropped to ~30k in use after new gw is live.

Jen (netops): Also applied a short-lived conntrack garbage-collection tweak: reduced tcp_timewait to 30s and increased ip_conntrack_max to 200k. Commands run:
```
echo 30 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_fin_timeout
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
```
Monitoring for side-effects.

Sophia: We notified affected customers and asked them to hold retries for 1 minute window. They're asking for RCA and ETA.

Ryan (oncall): Current status summary: mitigation in flight. Second NAT up, routing changed, conntrack limits raised, temporary throttles applied, two tenants rolled to hosted fallback. Error rate across private-inference-gw dropped from 30% -> 4% in 8m. Still watching.

IncidentBot: UPDATE: alert suppressed automatically after 8m.

Alex: Note — root cause seems to be ephemeral port exhaustion compounded by heavy retry loops from client SDKs and many short-lived connections creating conntrack churn. Secondary factors: single NAT per AZ and no port pooling on egress proxy.

Ryan (oncall): Next steps / ACTION items:
- Jen: validate conntrack tuning is safe and make changes idempotent in infra repo (PR) (assignee: Jen)
- Maria: Create a runbook entry for ephemeral port exhaustion for private deployments and add automated detection on SNAT port usage (assignee: Maria)
- Alex: Work with devex to update client SDK to use exponential backoff and jitter (assignee: Alex)
- Sophia: Draft customer-facing incident summary and timeline (assignee: Sophia)
- Ryan: Schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC.

Jen (netops): DONE: second NAT created, route table updated, conntrack tuning applied (temporary). Will open infra PR for permanent kernel params and test in staging.

Maria: DONE: applied temporary alert for ephemeral_ports_in_use > 75% and created dashboard panel.

Customer SRE: APPRECIATE the fast mitigation. Requesting periodic updates and the postmortem link.

Ryan (oncall): Closing thread for active intervention. Will re-open if error rate creeps above 5% or if new customer reports surface. Postmortem owners listed above. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
